subject.title: [Bug]: Browser interactions can exhaust model context by injecting too much page content

question: Should browser interactions default to compact, goal-shaped reads and post-action change reports, with raw/full page reads kept as an explicit escape hatch?
rationale: Current code already has caps, optional efficient mode, and overflow recovery, but making compact reads and action diffs the default changes the model-facing browser contract and compatibility expectations.

options.title: Adopt compact browser default
options.body: Make compact task-relevant browser output and small action change reports the default, with explicit raw/full snapshot requests for workflows that need the old shape.

options.title: Keep capped snapshots default
options.body: Treat the current 40,000-character cap plus optional efficient mode and docs as the supported mitigation until stronger live evidence justifies a default change.

options.title: Fold into broader browser roadmap
options.body: Decide this together with the open browser field-report work on stale refs, readiness hints, selectors, CAPTCHA signaling, and batch/action result semantics.

recommendation.title: Adopt compact browser default
recommendation.body: Make compact task-relevant browser output and small action change reports the default, with explicit raw/full snapshot requests for workflows that need the old shape.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history points most strongly to this handle for browser snapshot modes, default-mode config, and model-facing browser contract decisions.
